title: Who's Buying Your Florida Listing? How to Stage for Snowbirds, Families and Investors
summary: Stage your Florida listing for the buyers who actually shop there: snowbirds, families moving down and investors. Plus MLS photo rules.
body_markdown:
## First, does staging actually work?


Short answer: yes. Long answer, straight from the National Association of REALTORS:


- **83% of buyers' agents** say staging helps buyers picture the home as theirs
- **Almost half of sellers' agents** say it cut the time on market
- **29% of sellers' agents** saw offers go up by 1% to 10%
- **Photos are the #1 thing** buyers use on listing sites. 83% call them very useful


Not bad for a few pillows and a rug.


Sources: NAR[2025 Profile of Home Staging](https://www.nar.realtor/sites/default/files/2025-05/2025-profile-of-home-staging-05-06-2025.pdf) and[2025 Home Buyers and Sellers Generational Trends](https://www.nar.realtor/sites/default/files/2025-04/2025-home-buyers-and-sellers-generational-trends-04-01-2025.pdf) .


Buyer 1: the snowbird


## Meet Linda from Michigan


Linda (a made-up name for this blog) has shoveled her last driveway. She wants a winter home in Florida (Florida winter: when locals wear a hoodie at 65 degrees), somewhere that feels like vacation the minute she drops her suitcase.


She also wants to lock the door in April and not think about it again until November. Low fuss, high sunshine.


And Linda has company. Florida is the top U.S. state for foreign buyers, and Canadians are the biggest group of foreign buyers in the country. Hi, Ontario.


**So show Linda a living room that says "you're on vacation now."**


Before


After


That's the **Palms** bundle in the living area, with **Coral** adding the round table by the kitchen. Two bundles, one open floor plan, zero furniture trucks.


Then show her where she'll spend every afternoon. Stage the lanai with **Sanibel** or **Siesta Key** , and the Florida room with **Bloomray** . If the photo makes her forget she ever owned a snow shovel, you nailed it.


Buyer 2: the family


## Meet the Garcias, moving down from Ohio


The Garcias (also made up, also lovely) have two kids, one dog, a new job in Tampa, and a moving truck booked for July. (Brave.)


They're house hunting from a thousand miles away, and they're not alone: 43% of buyers start by scrolling listings online. Your photos are basically their first showing.


**Mom wants a bedroom that feels like a getaway.** The **Shoreline** bundle gets her there, minus the sand in the sheets.


Before


After


**Dad wants to know where Sunday pancakes happen.** An empty corner by the kitchen leaves him guessing. The **Seagrass** bundle answers with a long wood table and room for everyone.


Before


After


**The kids just want to know which room is theirs.** So stage every main room, not only the living room. Shoot more than one angle (the furniture stays the same in every shot), and add a 360 view or a property video so the Garcias can tour the house from their couch in Columbus.


Buyer 3: the investor


## Meet Dave, who has a spreadsheet


Dave is made up too, but his spreadsheet feels very real. Dave loves his spreadsheet. Dave says he's only in it for the rental income. Dave will also post a sunset photo the day he closes.


**So show Dave the money:**


- A condo bedroom staged cozy and hotel style, so it screams "book me"
- A spare room shown two ways: guest room and home office
- A pool area that sells itself. **Tahiti** brings the big umbrella, and **Harborside** or **Breeze** set the table by the water


Staging the same room twice costs a few dollars. Renting furniture twice costs... well, Dave already ran that number.


## Paint it Florida (but not flamingo pink)


Linda, the Garcias and Dave agree on one thing: a Florida home should look like Florida. Think ocean, palms and a really good sunset.


**Ocean blue** *Like the Gulf at noon*


**Sea glass** *Soft and breezy*


**Palm green** *Fresh and tropical*


**Coral** *A happy pop*


**Sand** *Warm and calm*


**Shell white** *Bright and clean*


**Rattan** *Natural and relaxed*


Keep the walls light and sprinkle two or three of these into pillows, art and rugs. The Florida bundles already do it for you, so feel free to take the credit.


More Florida bundles to try: Marina and Beachcomber for living rooms, Cove and Salt for bedrooms. And we keep adding new ones, so check back.


## The boring (but important) part


Good news: Florida doesn't have a special law for staged photos like California's new 2026 one. Less good news: state law still says ads can't mislead, with fines up to $5,000 each, and most Florida MLSs have their own rules.


The rule most agents miss


Stellar, Beaches and Miami MLS don't allow words or logos on listing photos. So "virtually staged" goes in your listing, not on the picture. Copy this into the start of your public remarks:


One or more photo(s) was virtually staged.


Then add "Virtually staged" to each staged photo's description. Done.


Adding a sofa, a rug or patio chairs? Great. Hiding cracks, swapping floors or adding a view that isn't there? Not great. Staging can add a sofa. It can't turn the parking lot into an ocean view.


Posting on Instagram or your own website? There, a label is your friend. Apply Design can add "Virtually staged" and your logo as a watermark.


## And now, the part your seller will love


Rented furniture bills you every month the house sits. Online staging is paid once, and nobody has to carry a sofa up three flights in July.


Furniture rental Auto Staging


Cost $4,000 to $6,000 From $7 a photo


Ready in Days About 10 minutes


Lasts 45 to 60 days, then more fees Yours to keep


New look Start over Change it anytime


Rental prices are U.S. averages for an empty home.


## Still wondering?


Can I use virtual staging on a Florida listing?


Absolutely. Just say the photos are staged, and don't change the home itself. No hiding damage and no imaginary ocean views.


Is there a Florida law about edited listing photos?


Not as of November 2026. California has one, Florida doesn't. The usual rule still applies: real estate ads can't be misleading.


Where do I write that a photo is virtually staged?


In the photo description and at the start of your public remarks. Most big Florida MLSs don't allow words or logos on the photo itself.


Does staging really help a home sell?


Yes. In NAR's 2025 staging report, 83% of buyers' agents said staging helps buyers picture the home as theirs, and almost half of sellers' agents said it cut time on market.


What does Apply Design cost?


Staging starts at $7 a photo, and your first one is free. That's cheaper than a flamingo lamp.


General info only, not legal advice. Based on Florida law and MLS rulebooks as of November 2026.[Read Stellar MLS's staging rule](https://rules.stellarmls.com/article/article-0404-virtually-staged-photos) or ask your broker.
